title: Canonical component of a compactification refinement
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring, $f:X\to Y$ a scheme morphism, and $c=(i_c,p_c)$ and $d=(i_d,p_d)$ compactifications with quasi-compact open immersions. Let $h:d\to c$ be a boundary-preserving refinement in the category of [det-nagata-definition-refinement]. For an arbitrary object $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_X})$, let $e_{h,K}:D(i_{c!})K\to Rh_*D(i_{d!})K$ and $\gamma_{h,p_c}:R(p_c\circ h)_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_{c*}Rh_*$ be the canonical open-adjunction refinement map and derived direct-image compositor of [def-sf-comp-refinement-data]. Using $F_c=Rp_{c*}D(i_{c!})$ and $F_d=Rp_{d*}D(i_{d!})$ from [def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek-compactification], define $\rho_{h,K}:F_c(K)\to F_d(K)$ to be the composite of $Rp_{c*}(e_{h,K})$, the component of $\gamma_{h,p_c}^{-1}$ at $D(i_{d!})K$, and the canonical equality identification $R(p_c\circ h)_*=Rp_{d*}$ from the refinement triangle. Neither compactification is required to be dense. This is the specified composite on the ordinary ambient derived categories, with no choice of an isomorphism.

source.place: Part (1): canonical compactification comparison with the identity compactification of a proper morphism.

proof.text: The canonical underived equality isomorphism lowerStarCongr, after right derivation, equals the functor equality isomorphism: perform equality induction on the structural triangle, then the derived identity calculation. Thus the displayed composite is precisely the specified canonical component.
